Authorized the President to use force under U.N. Security Council Resolution 678 to expel Iraqi forces from Kuwait, after a presidential determination that diplomatic means had been exhausted.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 105 Stat. 3](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/105/3){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 50 U.S.C. 1541 note](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/1541?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Sec. 2(a): authority to use force pursuant to Security Council Resolution 678.
- Sec. 2(b): required a presidential determination to Congress before force was used.
- Sec. 2(c): declared itself specific statutory authorization under the War Powers Resolution.

## Why it matters

It is the clearest modern case of Congress authorizing force to carry out a Security Council mandate, which ties it to the [UN Participation Act](unpa-1945.qmd). The close Senate vote (52 to 47) is often cited as the last seriously contested war vote before 2002.

## Current status

Repealed together with the 2002 Iraq authorization by the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (Pub. L. 119-60), signed December 18, 2025.

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Specific authorization. Laws aimed at a particular conflict, country, program, or problem. Most work through a framework statute: an AUMF through the War Powers Resolution, a sanctions act through IEEPA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Builds on.** [War Powers Resolution](wpr-1973.qmd).
- **Codified in.** [Title 50 U.S.C.](title50-usc.qmd).
